summary: An investigation of card C05061-K1 was initiated following an analyst alert regarding coordinated losses across multiple cards. Between January 12 and January 14, 2017, three unauthorized online product C transactions (3660106, 3660107, 3660108) totaling $2,189.02 were conducted on the card. These transactions utilized new devices (D009708 and D009709) routing through an anonymous proxy, representing a complete deviation from the card's 34-transaction historical baseline. Graph analysis revealed that peer cards C11543-K2 and C07212-K2 experienced identical proxy-masked product C purchase runs using sequentially provisioned device IDs (D009706 through D009709). Card C05061-K1 also carries prior confirmed fraud history, including closed case CC-2420. Based on these findings, the activity was confirmed as card-not-present new-device fraud, resulting in a card block, case creation, and regulatory filing.
open_question: While the sequential device provisioning and transaction batching strongly demonstrate an orchestrated card-not-present attack across C05061-K1, C11543-K2, and C07212-K2, direct cardholder confirmation would definitively verify that these online charges were unauthorized.
